picks.title: The terminal became my canvas
picks.excerpt: A designer's account of craft migrating off the visual canvas and into the terminal/CLI, where prompts and code (Claude Code-style agentic tooling) become the primary design surface. A concrete vibe-coding workflow shift rather than a taste essay.
picks.rationale: Most actionable card in the pool — a concrete account of design work moving into the terminal/CLI, changing how a designer actually tools up tomorrow.

picks.title: AX is just the orchestration layer
picks.excerpt: Reframes 'AX' (agent/AI experience) not as a new surface to decorate but as an orchestration layer designers must own — coordinating models, agents, and handoffs rather than hand-crafting each screen. A fresh Design-AX angle distinct from the 07-13 taste/handoff essays.
picks.rationale: Fresh framing of AX as an orchestration layer designers should own — a distinct thesis from yesterday's essays that reshapes how designers scope agentic work.

picks.title: Top logo designer quits because "AI is better than me"
picks.excerpt: Gary Simon (DesignCourse) reacts to a prominent logo designer publicly quitting with the line 'AI is better than me,' unpacking what the moment says about craft, identity, and where human designers still hold the edge.
picks.rationale: High-novelty creator-medium moment on craft vs AI — a distinct outlet and format that balances the essay-heavy pool.

picks.title: How a tiny Star Trek film team is rethinking VFX with AI
picks.excerpt: An indie Star Trek fan-film crew explains how generative AI could clear VFX's biggest bottleneck — green-screen keying and rotoscoping — pointing to where AI actually fits into a real production pipeline rather than replacing artists.
picks.rationale: Grounds the section in a real production pipeline — shows exactly where generative AI fits into VFX craft, adding a fourth distinct outlet and category.
